title: Studying abroad
text: Every year, thousands of students leave their home country to study in United Kingdom, Australia or Canada. Living in a new culture can be very excite, but many students also suffer of homesickness. When I arrived in Sydney, I was struggle with academic writing, and at first I could not understand what my lecturers saying. I also had to make my homework in a completely new way. Eventually, I asked to my tutor for help, and she showed me some useful strategies. Studying abroad is difficult, but it helps students become more independent.

errors.ruleReminder: Use the with country names that include words like Kingdom, States or Republic.
errors.explanation: United Kingdom contains the word Kingdom, so it needs the.

errors.ruleReminder: After be, use an adjective. Use -ing adjectives for the thing (exciting) and -ed for the feeling (excited).
errors.explanation: Excite is a verb. The culture causes the feeling, so we need the adjective exciting.

errors.ruleReminder: Suffer goes with from: suffer from an illness or a problem.
errors.explanation: The verb suffer is followed by from, not of.

errors.ruleReminder: Use was + -ing (was struggling) or the past simple (struggled), not was + base verb.
errors.explanation: Was struggle mixes two forms. Use struggled or was struggling.

errors.ruleReminder: Every clause needs a full verb. The -ing form needs be before it: were saying.
errors.explanation: Saying alone is not a full verb. It needs were: my lecturers were saying.

errors.ruleReminder: Some nouns go with one verb only. We do homework, do research and make a mistake.
errors.explanation: Homework goes with do: do my homework. Make my homework is not used.

errors.ruleReminder: Ask is followed directly by the person: ask someone for something.
errors.explanation: We ask someone for help. To is not needed after ask.
